name: Windsurf

Developers working on context-heavy tasks requiring persistent awareness across sessions

Install and launch the Windsurf IDE
Open a project or create a new one
Press Cmd/Ctrl+L or click the Cascade icon to open the AI assistant panel
usageNotes: Cascade offers three primary modes: 'Code' for autonomous changes, 'Plan' for multi-step planning, and 'Ask' for read-only analysis
Pricing is subscription-based with a quota system that replaced monthly credits. Free, Pro ($20/month), Teams ($40/seat/month), and Max ($200/month) plans are available
Quotas refresh daily/weekly, and unlimited Tab autocomplete does not consume quota
The tool is a proprietary standalone IDE, not a VS Code fork, so it has a smaller extension ecosystem
Features like Memories and Rules allow for persistent customization and context

Open an existing project or start a new one in the chat interface

name: Antigravity CLI
description: A terminal-based interface (TUI) for the Antigravity 2.0 agentic coding assistant, designed to help build, modify, test, and release Flutter applications, replacing the legacy Gemini CLI .
bestFor: Flutter and Dart developers seeking a terminal-based AI coding assistant for building and releasing applications
Users migrating from the legacy Gemini CLI
strengths: Terminal-based user interface (TUI) for a coding assistant
Supports automatic migration of settings from the legacy Gemini CLI
Respects workspace rules files like AGENTS.md for custom coding guidelines
gettingStarted: Install using one of the following commands: curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/install.sh | bash (macOS/Linux), irm https://antigravity.google/install.ps1 | iex (Windows PowerShell), or winget install Google.AntigravityCLI (Windows Command Prompt)

The first run will automatically check for and migrate settings from an existing Gemini CLI configuration
usageNotes: Replaces the legacy Gemini CLI for Dart and Flutter development
Supports local rules from .agents/skills/ or AGENTS.md, and maintains backward compatibility with GEMINI.md
Global settings and MCP server configurations are stored in ~/.antigravity/ (e.g., ~/.antigravity/mcp_config.json)

name: Grok Build

bestFor: Professional software engineers
Complex codebase tasks
End-to-end edit-run-test loops
Automated scripts and CI/CD pipelines
strengths: Supports custom model endpoints compatible with OpenAI API
Can operate in an interactive TUI, headlessly, or via ACP
Open-sourced CLI harness for developer inspection
Can coordinate workflows with up to 1,024 parallel agents
Compatible with Claude Code's configuration files (.claude/) for easier migration

Install via PowerShell on Windows: `irm https://x.ai/cli/install.ps1 | iex`
Authenticate by opening a browser on first launch, or set `XAI_API_KEY` environment variable
Start a session with `grok` in a project directory
usageNotes: Grok Build is available to SuperGrok and X Premium subscribers
Plan Mode maps out changes step-by-step for review before any code is written
User data retention for training is opt-in and off by default
Version 1.0 introduced expanded command-approval prompts for enhanced security

name: OpenCode
description: An open-source, terminal-first AI coding agent that acts as an interface between the user and various large language models. It provides tools for file management, shell access, and project planning to automate coding tasks .
bestFor: Developers who want a model-agnostic coding assistant
Users preferring a terminal-based or lightweight development environment
Developers seeking a local-first, privacy-focused AI tool for coding
Automating complex coding tasks with a plan/build workflow
strengths: Model-agnostic, supporting over 75 providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and local models via Ollama
Terminal-based TUI, desktop app (beta), and VS Code extension
Local-first operation, with code and conversation history stored locally by default
Offers a unique Plan/Build mode to plan changes before executing them
gettingStarted: Ensure Node.js (version 18 or higher) is installed
Install OpenCode using the install script: `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`, or via npm: `npm install -g opencode-ai`
Navigate to your project directory: `cd /path/to/your/project`
Set an API key as an environment variable (e.g., `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your-key-here`) or configure it interactively
Start OpenCode: `opencode`
usageNotes: It acts as a client for AI models, requiring users to bring their own API keys or use a provider like Pioneer
Uses a dual-mode workflow: 'Plan' mode (asks for permission before edits) and 'Build' mode (can read, write, and execute commands)
The `/connect` command is used to set up AI providers
Uses `AGENTS.md` file in the project root for persistent context about project structure and coding patterns
Supports `/undo` and `/redo` commands for version management
priceDetails: OpenCode itself is free and open-source; users pay for their own API usage from chosen model providers .

name: Cline
description: An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your IDE, capable of creating/editing files, running terminal commands, using a browser, and connecting to external tools with explicit user approval at every step .

strengths: Supports any model provider, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and local models via Ollama
Zero-trust architecture: runs client-side with no server-side code storage
Human-in-the-loop design requires explicit user approval for all sensitive actions
Includes browser automation for testing web apps and debugging
Extensible via Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers
Open-source with Apache 2.0 license
gettingStarted: Install the extension from the VS Code Marketplace or your IDE's extension marketplace
Connect your AI provider by adding your API key (e.g., from Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenAI) or configuring a local endpoint
Open the Cline sidebar and describe your task in natural language
usageNotes: Cline is free to use; users pay for their chosen model's API usage
Costs can be minimized by selecting cost-effective models and using context caching where available
Every file change and terminal command is shown as a diff and requires user approval
Can operate in a 'Plan' mode to explore the codebase without making changes
Supports @ mentions to reference files, folders, and URLs in prompts
Works with VS Code, Cursor, JetBrains, and via CLI

name: OpenHands
description: An open-source autonomous software engineering agent that can read an issue, write code, run tests, debug failures, and submit a pull request within a sandboxed environment . It functions as a self-hosted developer control center for running and automating coding agents and automations .
bestFor: Autonomous completion of well-scoped software engineering tasks
Teams seeking transparency and control over their AI coding agent
Running various AI agents (OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) via a unified interface
strengths: MIT licensed open-source platform
Flexibility to bring your own LLM (BYOK)
Ability to self-host locally, in Docker, on VMs, or in the cloud
High autonomous capability for end-to-end issue resolution
gettingStarted: Ensure prerequisites are met: Node.js 22.12.x or later and `uv`
Install the Agent Canvas globally using npm: `npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas`
Start the local stack with the command: `agent-canvas`
usageNotes: The agent operates in a sandboxed Docker environment with access to a terminal, code editor, browser, and file system by default .
Can be run directly on the host machine without a sandbox, but this gives the agent full filesystem access .
Supports integrations with third-party services like Slack, GitHub, Notion, and Linear for automations .
Supports the Agent-Client Protocol (ACP), allowing it to run other compatible agents .
A hosted SaaS version (app.all-hands.dev) is available with a free tier that uses your own API keys .
priceDetails: Freemium. Self-hosted open-source core is free (MIT). A free SaaS tier is available with BYOK or at-cost model pricing. Enterprise plans with features like RBAC and SSO are quote-based .
